narrative.overview:
Open Market is a sales chat that shows its work. The customer's words sit in a warm cream bubble; the advisor's answer is plain prose with no bubble around it; under the answer lies the real trace of what the agent opened, and beside it float the cart and the billing details the agent is filling in. It is not a chatbot widget. The page is the whole conversation, and everything on it is either something said or evidence for it.

The ground is quiet paper, the ink is near black, and one cacao brown carries every action. Density is that of a working tool: compact rows, small tabular figures, hairlines instead of panels. Warmth comes from the neutrals, which are all tinted toward clay, and from soft corners. Nothing is decorative: the only imagery is the customer's own photo.

Depth is reserved for what floats. The thread stays flat, so a card or a dock bubble reads at once as something beside the conversation, not part of it.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground, white only where something floats or takes input.
One brown for action, always paired with cream.
Answers as bare prose at reading width; only the customer speaks in a bubble.
Traces, hairlines and tabular figures as the visible proof.
Soft corners, with one small corner on the speaker's side of the bubble.
Light and dark follow the system; there is no theme switch.

rules.name: The Cream On Cacao Rule
rules.body: Cacao fill wears cream, and customer cream wears cacao letters. In dark mode the pair inverts: cream fill, cacao icon. No other color goes on a cacao fill.

rules.name: The Fill Versus Text Rule
rules.body: Every state color has a fill and a text form. Fills only tint or dot; letters and icons always use the `-text` form. A new state brings both, and the text form reaches 4.5:1 on paper, white and the warm tints.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Borders, grounds and text neutrals are tinted toward clay in both modes. The cool tint exists only inside the light-mode shadows.

rules.name: The Eleven Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No text measures under 11px (0.6875rem): not a badge, not a stamp.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Mono is only for what a machine wrote: source paths, REPL step titles, Code and Output blocks. Words the advisor or the page says to a person are never mono.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Clock times, durations, tokens, quantities and prices use tabular numerals, so figures do not shift as a step's seconds count up or a line changes.

rules.name: The Shared Edges Rule
rules.body: The text, the bubble and the input share the same left and right edges, always. Opening a card moves neither: it floats over them, by the author's decision, and on narrower desktops it may cover the right of the column. Platform moves the thread.

rules.name: The Flat Thread Rule
rules.body: The customer's bubble, the answer and the trace have no shadow. A trace is a hairline outline on paper, so proof reads as part of the page, not as an object on it.

rules.name: The Speaker's Corner Rule
rules.body: The customer's bubble is fully round except for its top right corner, cut to `tail` on the speaker's side. The three-dot wait marks the agent's side the same way, at bottom left, and disappears when the answer arrives.

rules.name: The Folded Proof Rule
rules.body: The trace is open while the turn runs and folds when it ends, staying folded. The toggle carries the count ("Show trace · 9 steps"), so the proof is one click away and the conversation stays readable.

rules.name: The Honest Cut Rule
rules.body: A step the stream never closed is muted "cut off", in Bark at medium weight, never red and never "failed". The page stopped seeing it, which does not mean it failed.

rules.name: The Three Ways Out Rule
rules.body: On desktop the card closes with Esc, its close button or its dock bubble, and clicking the thread leaves it open, so the visitor can read and scroll beside it. As a sheet it also closes on the scrim and by dragging down.

dos: Do put cream on cacao, and cacao letters on customer cream.
Do use the `-text` form for any colored letter or icon.
Do keep answers as bare prose capped at 70ch.
Do keep the thread and the composer on the same edges in every state.
Do show what the page understood inside the customer's own bubble.
Do use tabular numerals for times, quantities and prices.
Do give every control 2.75rem on a coarse pointer.
Do take any new value from these tokens, in both modes.
donts: Don't put an answer in a bubble: the only agent-side bubble is the three-dot wait.
Don't put a shadow on the customer's bubble, the answer or the trace.
Don't put mono on anything a person is told.
Don't mark a cut step as failed, or color it red.
Don't unfold the trace after a turn on its own.
Don't close the desktop card on an outside click.
Don't show a step, a percentage or a progress bar that the stream did not send.
Don't take an orange primary or a white customer bubble from platform's `DESIGN.md`: its stylesheet moved on and so did this page.
Don't use cool greys for borders, grounds or text.
